Let’s dive into Chapter 6: Setting Big, Hairy, Audacious Goals—Ambition as a Catalyst.
Have you ever noticed how the most enduring organizations aren’t afraid to set truly bold goals? I’m talking about those Big, Hairy, Audacious Goals—what we call BHAGs. These aren’t your everyday targets or easy wins. Instead, they’re clear, compelling challenges that push everyone in the organization way past their comfort zone.
Think of a BHAG like a mountain far off in the distance. It’s massive, a bit intimidating, and you can’t help but notice it. To reach the top, everyone has to pull together, pushing each other to new heights. The idea isn’t to take wild risks, but to pick a goal that’s both meaningful and tough enough to spark incredible effort.
Picture a company that sets out to become the leader in a brand-new technology, or one that’s determined to deliver a level of service the industry’s never seen before. That’s the kind of ambition we’re talking about.
So, how do the best organizations make these big goals actually work? Well, first, they make sure the goal is crystal clear—so everyone knows exactly what success looks like. Then, they connect the goal to their core purpose and values, so it feels real and genuinely motivating.
Here’s another key: they break that huge mountain into smaller hills—milestones that make progress visible and tangible. And, along the way, they celebrate those wins, keeping the momentum and excitement alive.
Take a real-world example. Imagine a company that commits to eliminating all waste from its operations in ten years, or another that aims to serve a billion customers around the globe. These aren’t goals anyone can guarantee or achieve overnight, but they bring people together with a sense of adventure and possibility.
The true power of a BHAG is in how it focuses everyone’s energy and attention. It gives teams something to rally around, sparks creative solutions, and helps organizations push through tough challenges. Over time, chasing these ambitious goals becomes part of who they are—a culture built on striving and achievement.
So, here’s the key takeaway: the companies that last don’t just settle for small, safe steps. They aim high, using bold, audacious goals to drive progress and fire up their people. When that kind of ambition is grounded in real values and purpose, it becomes a powerful engine for long-term success.
